feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: Trump withdraws Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, as his nominee to lead ICE
entry.summary: The White House says it is withdrawing its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to lead ICE, ensuring that an agency at the forefront of President Trump's domestic agenda will remain without a Senate-confirmed leader for at least a while longer.

entry.title: ICE agent appears in Minnesota court to face charges in the shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant
entry.summary: Christian Castro, a federal immigration officer, made his first court appearance in Minnesota since he was booked Wednesday into a local jail. Castro faces multiple state and federal charges in connection with a shooting during the immigration surge in Minnesota.

entry.title: Retired Olympic superstar Jessie Diggins wins her first-ever 100 mile trail race
entry.summary: This spring Jessie Diggins retired as one of America's most successful winter Olympic athletes at age 34. She's relaxing by entering 100-mile trail running races and navigating what comes next.

entry.title: To prevent deaths in childbirth, Kenyan moms turn to an AI powered chatbot
entry.summary: Many questions come up during pregnancy. Is swelling normal? Are avocados safe to eat? For folks in Kenya who don't have a search engine at their fingertips, a chatbot is offering a lifeline.

entry.title: A year ago, President Trump pledged to lower Medicaid drug prices. Has that happened?
entry.summary: The Trump administration's efforts to lower drug prices included promised changes to Medicaid. But it's still unclear which drugs will be affected. And each state has to opt in.

entry.title: 'American Scoundrel' traces Roy Cohn's playbook from McCarthyism to Trump
entry.summary: In Kai Bird's biography of Cohn, he looks at how the lawyer taught Trump how to deny, delay, attack, sue and countersue, never admit defeat, side-step paying bills and avoid a paper trail.

entry.title: Greetings from Beijing, where baozi are worth the wait in line
entry.summary: The popular fluffy steamed buns are filled with pork, vegetables, tofu — and in one trendy Beijing shop, chocolate and red beans.

entry.title: U.N.-backed experts cite possible U.S. war crimes in Iran, including a school attack
entry.summary: Human rights experts commissioned by the U.N. say they have found "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes in Iran, including a strike on a school in the southern city of Minab.

entry.title: The Fed raises interest rates. And, EU proposes Canada become an 'associate member'
entry.summary: The Federal Reserve has raised interest rates for the first time in years. And, the European Union has proposed that Canada become its first-ever "associate member."

entry.title: Pressure on global chokepoints drives Asia's increased use of Arctic Trade Routes
entry.summary: Asian nations began pilot voyages over a decade ago to find routes to Europe and the Middle East that were faster and less vulnerable to chokepoints. The ongoing war has added impetus to those efforts.
